entry.title: Minimizing data requirements for chemical and material property prediction via cluster-based training set selection
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01076-9 A survey of 100 algorithms across 60 chemical and materials property prediction tasks finds that cluster-based selection of training data outperforms active learning, and a theoretical framework establishes why this occurs in the low-data limit.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science

entry.title: Cognitive grounding improves LLM simulation of collective human behavior
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01080-z The study shows that guiding AI agents with descriptions of how people make decisions in a supply-chain game helps agents reproduce collective human behavior.

entry.title: Training reservoirs without looking back
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01079-6 By training a reservoir computing system without access to its intermediate states and by eliminating the coupling between its nodes, a physical learning framework achieves efficient learning both in simulation and on optoelectronic hardware.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science
